newsitem.title: UK: London July coffee futures tumble after rally.
newsitem.headline: London July coffee futures tumble after rally.

text.p: London robusta coffee futures tumbled in early trade on Monday with benchmark July opening a sharp $270 down to $2,200 per tonne as the market took a sharp reverse from last week's spectacular rally.

The slide followed a steep 12-percent fall in New York on Friday on frantic speculative selling. By 0850 GMT, the London first-month contract fell further by $330 to $2,140. This compares with last week's 20-month-peak of $2,670.

The sell-off in New York ahead of the weekend took some of the air out of the most spectacular bubble in the coffee market in 20 years. The July contract fell 38.40 cents per lb to close at 276.40, a decline of 12 percent in one day.

"It's foolish to think a market goes in only one direction," said Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes. "When it rises that much, the pullbacks are going to be more severe. Moves like this take your breath away."
Coffee's run-up since early January was fuelled by depleting consumer and producer stocks, supply problems from Colombia and expectations of a lower Brazilian harvest.

A winter frost in Brazil in the coming weeks could also dent supply prospects from the world's largest grower. June and July are the frost danger months. No damaging cold is expected this week in Brazil's coffee belt.
